note: Balanced curated X chatter for Politics world; lean describes the account.

posts.name: Decision Desk HQ
posts.text: Last night was the largest blue wave in a generation. Democrats have been projected as winner in 54 Senate seats, flipping seven states and with a lead in two others (Alaska and Mississippi). In the House, Democrats have been projected in 249 seats - a net gain of 38 so far.

posts.name: Decision Desk HQ
posts.text: Sherrod Brown was projected the winner of Ohio's Senate race. Compared to the 2024 Senate contest, which Brown narrowly lost, every county in the state shifted left.

posts.name: Nate Silver
posts.text: OK, wrote about the models vs. prediction markets debate. Actually, the real stolen valor is from NYT/Siena. But prediction markets converged toward FLIPR/model prices, not the other way around, and the models got to the right answer sooner and more confidently.

posts.name: Sean Trende
posts.text: In the Trump era, Texas Republicans had been winning a game of chicken where either their support levels among Hispanics, suburbanites, or the overall political environment kept them afloat. On Tuesday all three factors went the other way.

posts.name: Sean Trende
posts.text: I will probably write this up later without the GPT generated chart, and causation is always very difficult to prove but the intuition that the VRA redistricting supercharged Black turnout in the south seems to hold up reasonably well at first look.

posts.name: Matthew Yglesias
posts.text: Conservative pundits reacting to Republicans fucking up the economy so badly that Democrats overcome a hideously biased senate map and brutal mid-Census House gerrymanders: "Dumb libs sure were hysterical about the state of American democracy."

posts.name: Matthew Yglesias
posts.text: 2026 was the year AIPAC lost its clout in Democratic primaries, then pro-Israel groups tried to panic Jews everywhere into voting Republican, then JD Vance responded to the wipeout by assigning sole responsibility to the Iran policy they pushed for.

posts.name: Aaron Rupar
posts.text: New in PN: The only thing Democrats have to fear is fear itself — even though affordability was the top campaign issue, if Democrats take only a narrow lesson from the most sweeping midterm victory in half a century they will undershoot the moment.

posts.name: Aaron Rupar
posts.text: El-Sayed: "People have always seen Donald Trump as this big monster that's unbeatable. It turns out, you just stand up to him, and he can read the tea leaves. I'm willing to work with anyone ... it should never be about retribution. It's about enforcing the rule of law..."

posts.name: Erick Erickson
posts.text: Were I a ranking Republican in the House or Senate, I’d start taking the Trump family corruption seriously and cooperate in grown up investigations. 90% of voters said corruption was a determining factor in their vote and over 60% pointed not to Somali fraud or highspeed rail,

posts.name: Erick Erickson
posts.text: Two Senators tell me the Vice President is right that the GOP turned against the Iran war in the Senate GOP’s own polling. But they say what the VP leaves out is that the turn came after the VP negotiated a bad deal with the Iranian regime that repulsed the GOP.

posts.name: Guy Benson
posts.text: A mystical feeling has washed over me in the last 24 hours that the institution of the United States Senate is no longer a pressing threat to democracy. These energies may again evolve circa 2032.

posts.name: Rich Lowry
posts.text: On the Iran war, of course, it hurt Republicans badly on Tuesday. The war was never popular, Trump hasn’t won it, and it increased fuel costs for everyone in the country. That’s not a formula for political success in the run-up to midterms.

posts.name: Erick Erickson
posts.text: Few things have inspired black voters to vote across the South more than Trump’s redistricting initiative to wipe out black voting districts. Even in states that didn’t do it, the threat of it mobilized black voters more than anything in recent decades.
